book_title: Chapter 8: Reading the Tape — Stage 4 Breakdown & Multi-Timeframe Structure
question: Does the price chart support holding or buying ANET after Friday's 11.57% plunge, and how do the daily, weekly, and 4-hour timeframes align?

epigraph.quote: The tape tells all, if only we know how to read it.
epigraph.author: Jesse Livermore

web_blocks.html: On November 20, 2026, Arista Networks fell 11.57% to close at $167.66 ($167.62 in Finviz) [22][23]. That capped an 18.17% weekly drop. The selloff sliced right through our $172.09 stop. On the weekly chart (1W), shares sit 8.37% below the 10-week EMA ($182.98). Price also sits 5.69% below the 30-week SMA ($177.78) and below the 40-week EMA ($170.86), with weekly RSI at 46.41 [23]. On the daily chart (1D), shares trade 12.68% below the 50-day SMA ($192.01) and 7.97% below the 20-day SMA ($182.15). Daily price also slipped 0.55% below the 200-day SMA ($168.58), with daily RSI at 41.49 and a -0.56 (Strong Sell) TradingView rating [23]. On the 4-hour chart (4H), price trails the 20-EMA ($184.95) and 50-SMA ($181.43) with 4H RSI at 36.74.

Two internal trend classifiers split on this session, so we disclose both. Our quantitative ledger (facts_US_2026-11-20.json) labels ANET as Stage 1 (Basing) (stage: 1). It bases that tag on $167.62 sitting 0.73 ATRs above the 63-day low ($158.35) after an earlier 0.43 volume dry-up. By contrast, our Weinstein snapshot engine (snapshots_US_2026-11-20.json) tags ANET as STAGE_4 (CAP_REJECTED, AVOID_STAGE4_OR_BROKEN). Price broke the 30-week SMA ($177.78), 50-day SMA ($192.01), and 200-day SMA ($168.58) on 13.85 million shares. That volume was 1.67x the 30-day average of 8.31 million shares (2.19x Finviz relative volume) [22][23]. Heavy-volume breaks below major averages signal distribution, not safe basing. The stricter STAGE_4 (CAP_REJECTED) rule governs here. New capital stays sidelined, and the $172.09 stop breach forces an immediate exit on held shares.

web_blocks.title: 8.2 Downtrend Macro Backdrop, Distribution & Options Convexity Check

web_blocks.html: The broader market tape also calls for defense. U.S. equities shifted from a Correction into a Downtrend. The S&P 500 sits 11.6% off its highs with 10 distribution days in 25 sessions. SPY closed at $689.81 (-3.64% 1D, -8.56% 1W, RSI 24.91) on 2.88x 20-day average volume. QQQ fell to $608.45 (-5.67% 1D, -10.51% 1W, RSI 26.63) on 2.59x volume. Only 34.5% of monitored stocks hold above their 50-day SMA, and 41.8% sit above their 200-day SMA. Just 1 of 11 S&P sectors holds above its 20-day average, and 3 of 11 hold above their 50-day average. Hedging demand jumped, pushing the Cboe total put/call ratio to 1.13 and SPX put/call to 1.41 [27].

web_blocks.takeaway: Every timeframe from 4H to 1W confirms a Stage 4 break below key averages on 1.67x volume. Even at Pivot S1 ($149.07–$153.61), a genuine 1.56x ATR14 structural stop at Pivot S2 ($133.83) fails 1.50:1 R:R against $180.00 ex-SBC fair value.

web_blocks.title: 8.3 Institutional Ownership, Insider Activity & Options Playbook

web_blocks.html: Ownership trends match the weak chart. Institutions hold 73.89% of shares (-1.54% quarterly change), and insiders hold 16.66% (-3.47% quarterly change) [22]. Recent filings show steady Q4 selling while buybacks stayed at zero. Co-founder Andreas Bechtolsheim sold 300,000 shares on November 18 under Rule 10b5-1 [31][32]. CEO Jayshree Ullal sold 715,909 shares in October and gifted 890,000 shares on November 17 [33]. Director Lewis Chew also sold 2,500 shares on November 13 outside a 10b5-1 plan [34]. Short interest stays low at 1.14% of float (12.03 million shares, 1.90 days to cover), showing long-only selling drove the drop [22]. Options also show NO_OPTIONS_EDGE. A $165/$180 bull call spread costs $6.75 for $8.25 max gain (1.22:1 R:R, below our 1.25:1 floor), and the 4-hour chart has not turned up.

book_paragraphs: Price charts exist to keep your emotions from overriding your risk discipline. One week ago, Arista Networks sat above every key moving average and looked like the last sturdy pillar in AI networking. Five trading sessions later, the tape has spoken unmistakably. On November 20, 2026, shares plunged 11.57% on 13.85 million shares—1.67 times normal 30-day volume—to close at $167.66, capping an 18.17% weekly drop.

That single session broke our locked $172.09 structural stop and pushed the stock below its 50-day average ($192.01), its 30-week average ($177.78), and its 200-day average ($168.58) all at once. Because two internal models view the bar differently, we spell out the split plainly: our quantitative facts ledger labels ANET Stage 1 Basing because it remains 0.73 ATRs above its 63-day low of $158.35, while our Weinstein snapshot engine tags it Stage 4 (CAP_REJECTED) because price broke the 30-week and 50-day averages on heavy distribution. In a 10-distribution-day market downtrend, the stricter Stage 4 rule governs.

book_subsections.title: Why the 4-Hour, Daily, and Weekly Charts All Say Stand Aside
paragraphs: Look across every timeframe and the message is identical: sellers remain in control. On the weekly chart, Arista sits 8.37% below its 10-week exponential average ($182.98) and 5.69% below its 30-week simple average ($177.78), with weekly RSI down to 46.41. On the daily chart, price sits 12.68% beneath its 50-day average ($192.01) with daily RSI at 41.49 and a 14-day Average True Range of $12.68—meaning 7.5% daily swings are live noise.

Even the tactical 4-hour chart shows zero evidence of stabilization. Price sits nearly 10% below the 4-hour 20-EMA ($184.95), 4-hour RSI is sliding at 36.74, and our intraday turn indicator remains false. Meanwhile, the S&P 500 is in an official Downtrend with 10 distribution days, SPY daily RSI down at 24.91, and Cboe total put/call spiking to 1.13. Trying to catch a 2.43-beta networking stock mid-air during a market-wide tech liquidation violates every rule of Stage 2 investing.

book_subsections.title: Reading Ownership Flow and Standing Down on Options
paragraphs: Short interest sits at just 1.14% of float—12.03 million shares, or under two days of volume—so Friday's collapse was not a hedge-fund short raid. Instead, institutional ownership edged down 1.54% while insiders trimmed 3.47% across Q4 Form 4 and Form 144 filings as corporate share buybacks remained paused at zero. That tells you long-only funds and insiders are lightening exposure at the same time.

We also checked whether listed call options offer a defined-risk rebound trade and rejected the idea. A $165/$180 bull call spread costs $6.75 for at most $8.25 of upside—only 1.22-to-1 reward-to-risk, below our 1.25-to-1 threshold—and the 4-hour chart has not turned up. Even if shares pull back toward Pivot S1 ($149.07–$153.61), the $12.68 daily ATR and 2.43 beta make a tight $145.00 stop (0.68x ATR) untenable; placing a realistic 1.56x ATR stop at Pivot S2 ($133.83) leaves just 1.33-to-1 reward-to-risk against our $180.00 ex-SBC Base value, while waiting for a $177.78 reclaim leaves only 0.05-to-1.

book_subsections.title: Reconciling the Two Stage Classifiers Without Self-Deception
paragraphs: You will notice a split between our two technical engines on November 20, and it deserves a direct explanation. The quantitative facts ledger labels ANET Stage 1 Basing because $167.62 sits 0.73 ATRs above its 63-day swing low of $158.35 after a quiet volume dry-up earlier in the autumn. Meanwhile, our Weinstein snapshot engine tags ANET as Stage 4 (CAP_REJECTED) because price broke beneath both the falling 50-day average ($192.01) and the 30-week average ($177.78).

Why follow the Stage 4 tag instead of clinging to Stage 1? Context settles the tie. Friday's 11.57% plunge occurred on 13.85 million shares—1.67 times normal volume—breaking the 200-day moving average ($168.58) alongside heavy distribution across the S&P 500 and Nasdaq. Treating an active heavy-volume breakdown as a safe base invites avoidable losses.

book_subsections.title: What a Real Stage 1 Base Looks Like From Here
paragraphs: With a 1-year beta of 2.43 and a $12.68 daily Average True Range, Arista rarely stops falling in a single session. A genuine Stage 1 base requires weeks of sideways price action where sellers run out of supply, daily swings narrow below Pivot S1 ($149.07–$153.61) without breaching Pivot S2 ($133.83), and red-day volume dries up below the 8.31 million share average.

Even then, disciplined investors wait for proof rather than guessing the exact bottom. A confirmed Stage 2 resumption requires the 4-hour 20-EMA to turn upward, daily RSI to climb back above 50, and price to reclaim the 30-week moving average ($177.78) on volume at least 1.3 times average. Until that sequence plays out, patience costs nothing.
